agent.problem: The stop relies too heavily on discovery questions rather than informed picks. Cards 2 and 4 already require knowledge of details not yet disclosed, and cards 6, 8 and 12 likewise cannot be reasoned from their setups: nothing indicates whether Jesus stays seated, that He washes feet, or what consequence He announces. This makes much of the stop a guessing game.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The blank asks for 'feet,' wording the baker has not seen and cannot reason out from the preceding card about Jesus' garments and towel. The passage title does not supply the required earlier-card reasoning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The question's 'them' has no antecedent on the choice card. It relies on an earlier card to identify the disciples, so the question does not stand on its own when shown again for correction.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The phrase 'these things' points back to teachings on earlier cards without identifying them. The question needs to supply the context of following Jesus' example and doing what He has taught.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The phrases 'all this' and 'it' depend on the preceding cards about Jesus' chosen ones and the Scripture concerning His betrayer. Without that context, the question does not say what Jesus is telling the disciples beforehand.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The card cites John 13:20, but its Bible action, Jesus reclining at the table again, comes from John 13:12. The continuation line can stand without repeating that earlier detail; as written, the citation does not match what the card uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

human.problem: The card rewords John 13:19 'you will believe that I am He' into third person as 'they will ___ that He is He.' That reads unclearly and loses the 'I am He' wording. The card also says 'telling them all this' where the text says 'telling you now before it happens', which may widen what 'it' refers to.
human.question: When a choice card puts Jesus' 'I am He' sayings into third person, should it quote the BSB wording ('believe that I am He') instead of rewording it as 'He is He'? Does 'all this' count as stretching an open 'it'?
